title: What If a Flood Wrapped Whole Trees in Spider Webs?

scenes.text: What if millions of spiders took over the trees? After one flood in Pakistan, they did.
In July 2010, monsoon floods covered an area the size of England.
Spiders and other bugs, stranded by the rising water, climbed up into the trees.
They spun webs so thick that whole trees looked wrapped in cocoons, along farm fields in Sindh.
By December, about four months after the flood, the spiders were still there.
Villagers said there were fewer mosquitoes than expected, even with all that standing water.

description:
What if millions of spiders took over the trees?
After the 2010 floods in Pakistan, flooded fields were lined with trees wrapped in webs for months.
